summary: Iteration 28: Verified (1) extraction of UsersTab/CodesTab/CouponsTab from SuperAdminPanel (no regression — all data-testids render, sub-tabs open forms correctly, AdsTab still works, 5 other tabs load without pageerrors) and (2) Push notification behavior on POST /api/security/incidents — push_result key is PRESENT for severity='critical' and 'high', ABSENT for 'low' and 'medium'; compound_id of created incident matches reporter's compound (basis for admin-targeting query). Backend pytest: 6/6 passed.

minor.issue: When VAPID keys are set but no admin in the compound has push_subscriptions, push_result returns {total:0,sent:0,failed:0} — correct behavior but confirm product wants this surfaced vs suppressed in response. Currently response payload grows by ~60 bytes per critical/high incident even when nothing was sent.
UNRELATED to this iteration — global search returns 500 with log 'Search error: family_id' (KeyError). Pre-existing, surfaced as side-effect when test typed into navbar searchbox.

action_items: (Optional) Consider suppressing push_result from response when total==0 to keep payload minimal, or leave as-is (current test_iter28 locks in 'key present' contract which is desirable for clients).
Pre-existing: Fix /api/search 500 'Search error: family_id' (unrelated to iter28 but logged during testing).
Iter27 leftover: DELETE /api/security/incidents permission mismatch vs UI inc-delete button (not re-tested this round, still open).
critical_code_review_comments: security.py: create_security_incident correctly wraps push call in try/except so a push failure never breaks incident creation — good.

push_notification_service.send_broadcast_notification uses target_user_ids filter on push_subscriptions.user_id — correctly compound-isolated via admin_ids list built from db.users query with compound_id filter.

UsersTab/CodesTab/CouponsTab are clean single-responsibility components. Prop drilling from SuperAdminPanel is heavy (UsersTab: 11 props, CodesTab: 13 props, CouponsTab: 10 props) — consider a shared context or useReducer in parent for maintainability; not a blocker.
CouponsTab Create button onClick={handleCreateCoupon} is wired; disabled=!newCoupon.code.trim() prevents empty submits — correct.
CodesTab references fetchCodes/handleCreateCode/handleToggleCode/handleDeleteCode from parent — all confirmed present in SuperAdminPanel (1017 lines).

In push_notification_service.py send_broadcast_notification: if both target_user_ids and compound_id are given, query becomes AND — ok, but when compound_id is None (as in incident flow), admin_ids already pre-scoped upstream — correct.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on rendering/regression scope; form-submit→persistence flow covered by iter27 (known-good) and not re-asserted in iter28

seed_data_creation: Pytest creates + deletes TEST_iter28_* incidents (cleaned). UI scripting may have left a TEST_ITER28_X coupon attempt that did NOT persist (DB verified: 0 matches, only pre-existing WELCOME20 present). No cleanup needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Super-admin app route is /app/super-admin (with /app prefix). SuperAdmin role has isSuperAdminOnly filter hiding codes/coupons/user_subs/analytics — use Owner_homeme (app_owner role) to test those. Backend subscription-codes endpoint is /api/subscription-codes (returns {codes:[], stats:{}}); coupons endpoint is /api/coupons (returns {coupons:[], stats:{}}). Push incident contract: response.incident.push_result key present iff severity in ['high','critical']. Navbar has a global search input at the top — avoid using generic input[type='text'] selectors in Playwright; scope to specific data-testid or placeholder instead.
rca of the issue: No new issues. Push notification code path is correctly conditional on severity level. Compound isolation verified: admin_ids are built from db.users query filtered by incident.compound_id, then passed as target_user_ids to push_subscriptions — two-layer scoping (users → subscriptions) ensures no cross-compound leaks. Failures in individual webpush calls are swallowed per-subscription and aggregated into push_result.failed count; the outer try/except ensures incident creation itself never fails due to push issues.
